{"decision":"NOT DECIDED. Recorded so the options and their costs survive the session that found them.

The spec's prescription is a server-minted handle passed as an ordinary tool argument, and half of that already exists: `ClaimReq.seat` accepts a caller-supplied seat today, documented as "pass your own only if you have a durable handle for the session (a fleet worker name); it is a name, never a lock". What is undecided is how a client OBTAINS one and CARRIES it without every tool call growing a parameter no human should have to think about.

(a) A `hello`-style tool that mints and returns a seat, which the client then passes on the calls that care (claim_region, release_claim, the stale-seat check). Explicit, transport-independent, and inspectable. Cost: the agent has to remember it, and an agent that forgets silently gets fresh-seat behaviour again — the failure is quiet, which is the property this design most wants to avoid.

(b) Derive the seat from what a stateless request already carries. rmcp reconstructs a `ClientInfo` per request via `peer_info_for_stateless_request`, from headers. Cost: nothing in it is guaranteed stable or unique per client, so this trades a loud missing parameter for a quiet wrong answer.

(c) Accept one seat per server PROCESS on the sessionless transport. Cost: it is exactly the regression `req:seat-per-client` was written against — `claim_report` telling six sessions they are each other.

(d) Serve sessionless HTTP but refuse the claim family on it, directing those callers to stdio or a legacy version. Cost: honest and loud, and it makes `cap:remote-sessions` conditional on a protocol version — a real narrowing of what reflow2 offers.

Anthony's word is wanted on which. My recommendation is (a), with the refusal from (d) as its backstop: mint on request, and when a claim-family call arrives on a sessionless transport WITHOUT a seat argument, refuse it by name and say what would have worked, rather than silently minting a per-request seat and reporting success. That converts the quiet failure in (a) into a loud one, which is `req:no-silent-fallback` applied to identity.","name":"How a client obtains and carries its seat once the transport has no sessions — OPEN, awaiting Anthony","rationale":"Recorded at `proposed` deliberately. Anthony's word covered the UPGRADE ("I want to upgrade to rmcp v3.0.1"), not the shape of the seat fix, and `req:seat-identity-survives-stateless-mcp` itself says the open part is "deciding how a client obtains and carries the handle". Promoting this myself would forge his signature on a choice with four live options and real trade-offs (dec:certainty-derived).

Not urgent, and the measurement says why: `tools/stateless_seat_probe.py` shows one seat per client on stdio and on HTTP at 2025-06-18, and the transports actually in use — Claude Code and grok build over stdio — are unaffected. The 12-month feature-lifecycle window in the 2026-07-28 revision applies, and rmcp's own `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` is still `V_2025_11_25`, so no client reaches the broken path by default. It becomes urgent the moment a client negotiates 2026-07-28 against a shared `--http` server.

Composes with `dec:identity-out-of-band`, which already holds that names are assigned with zero coordination rather than derived from shared state — a server-minted handle is that same principle one layer up.","status":"proposed"}
